newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares linger in record territory.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares linger in record territory.

text.p: Egyptian shares lingered in record territory for the 22nd consecutive trading day when they rose on Wednesday in turnover led by Medinet Nasr Housing and Development.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) said the all-share index rose 1.97 points to 423.09 points in turnover worth 103 million pounds ($30 million).
"What's happening is there is a lot of profit-taking in the market and also this massive jump in prices took place in the last two months," said broker Sharif Cararah of Hermes EFG.
"It has come to an easing," he said of the 22-day bull run. "There is some relaxation, which is a natural phenomenon after a long rally."

Medinet Nasr shares had risen on Tuesday when investors realised they could still buy stocks and be eligible for a free share if they hold on to them until the end of March. The buying spree spilled over into Wednesday, when the shares rose 10 pounds to close at 520 in turnover of 16.8 million pounds.
"The period was extended for investors to be eligible for a bonus shares, so people got in again," said Cararah.

Public Enterprise Minister Atef Obeid was quoted on Wednesday as saying that he thought the share price had risen because large investors were accumulating shares in the hope that land prices would rise and that the stock might have risen beyond the value justified by its holdings of land.
Medinet Nasr shares were sold by the state at 65.00 pounds in a landmark privatisation last May.
Abu Qir Fertilisers and Chemical Industries was among the day's most active shares. It closed up 6.17 pounds to close at 129.73 in turnover worth 7.5 million, the CMA said.
"Abu Qir is a candidate for a GDR (global depositary receipt) which is the main reason, and investors think the expansion which will take place will be reflected in earnings next year," Cararah said.

Al-Ahram Beverages shares took a breather after the privatisation on Tuesday of 75 percent of the company, with the state selling 3.3735 million shares to the U.S-based Luxor Group. On Wednesday, its share price closed unchanged at 132.4 pounds in one transaction of 6,951 shares.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 732.93 points from 724.49 on Tuesday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms fell to 271.46 from 271.56 points.
Out of the 85 shares traded, 37 gained, 23 lost and 26 ended the day unchanged.
